   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS -

  MEMORANDUM

 TO:  Beverly Hills City Council Open BH
  Design and Operating Standards Subcommittee

 FROM:  Shana Epstein, Director of Public Works
  Daren Grilley, Assistant Director of Public Works, City Engineer
  Mandana Motahari, City Architect
  Laura Biery, Marketing and Economic Sustainability Manager

 DATE:  June 13, 2022

 SUBJECT:  Open BH Design and Operating Standards Subcommittee Stakeholder
  Outreach Meeting

 ATTACHMENTS:  1. Stakeholder Outreach & Involvement Diagram
  2. Topics of Small Groups Discussion

INTRODUCTION
This item provides the Councilmembers assigned to the Open BH Design and Operating
Standards Subcommittee (Subcommittee) with an outline of the discussion points for today’s
meeting. This stakeholder outreach meeting is one of several stakeholder outreach meetings that
will occur over the course of the next 6 months. For those that are not able to participate in today’s
outreach meeting, future outreach for the project will include online surveys and individual
conversations with current Open BH participants as well as sample interactive parklet designs.

DISCUSSION
Open BH was created to help all Beverly Hills businesses to be open during the pandemic, with
restaurant and café uses permitted to provide open-air dining as a temporary solution to help
them stay operational. Many of the parklet installations were done quickly and constructed with
easy to assemble materials to meet the temporary need for additional outdoor space during the
pandemic. The parklets often reflect the unique character and aesthetic of each business,
however, overall aesthetics are not cohesive. With the desire to make these temporary
installations permanent, parklets need to be inviting and create people-oriented spaces that are
functional, with aesthetic enhancements to the overall streetscape. To achieve this goal,
developing a set of minimum design standards is warranted with considerations to the Beverly
Hills brand.

The architectural firm of Lorcan O’Herlihy Architects (LOHA) has been engaged to provide design
consulting services for developing design guidelines for this effort.
 Meeting Date: June 13, 2022

The focus of this Subcommittee is to develop design and operational standards. For the purpose
of today’s meeting, staff will focus on the path and approach to develop design standards and
defer the operational standards discussions to a future meeting. Today’s agenda includes:

    A Brief Project History
    Existing Conditions of Parklets
    Project Goals
    Project Timeline
    Small Group Workshop

Today’s meeting will focus on a conversation with business owners and residents regarding the
current and future design of parklets for outdoor dining in the City.

FISCAL IMPACT
None at this time. To be evaluated at future meetings based on project development and
recommendations made by the Subcommittee.

RECOMMENDATION
Design will not commence until stakeholder input and feedback has been assessed, staff
recommends that the Subcommittee and stakeholders provide comments and discuss the
following questions:

  1. With the onset of COVID, new dining experiences like parklets were introduced as
  extensions to sidewalks, how did these outdoor dining spaces improve the sidewalk?
  How would you describe any unintended consequences?

  2. What words would you use to describe the identity of Beverly Hills? How can the identity
  of Beverly Hills be reflected in the design of permanent parklets?

  3. Given the proximity of the parklets to oncoming traffic, dining safety is an important
  design parameter. What effective safety measures have you observed, used, or would
  like to see?

  4. What else would you like us to consider as we develop the parklet guidelines?

Beverly Hills City Council Liaison /
  OpenBH Design and Operating Standards Ad Hoc Subcommittee
  Special Meeting #3

  CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 N. Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210

  Wednesday, June 13, 2022
  11:00 AM

  MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time: June 13, 2022 11:00AM

IN ATTENDANCE:

  Mayor Lili Bosse; Councilmember John Mirisch; Assistant City Manager Nancy Hunt-
  Coffey; Marketing & Economic Sustainability Manager Laura Biery; Special Events
  Coordinator Magdalena Davis; Director of Public Works Shana Epstein; Director of
  Community Development Ryan Gohlich; City Architect Mandana Motahari; City
  Engineer/Assistant Director of Public Works Daren Grilley; Assistant Director
  Community Development Building Official David Yelton; City Planner Timothea Tway;
  Associate Project Manager Public Works Ji Kim; Lorcan O’Herlihy of O’Herlihy
  Architects; Kevin Murray of O’Herlihy Architects; Ghazaleh Khezi of O’Herlihy
  Architects; President & CEO of Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce Todd Johnson;
  David Miharooni of Brickstar Capital; Daniel Miharooni of Brickstar Capital; Beverly
  Hills Chamber of Commerce Greg Sefain; Bianca Heyward of the Beverly Hills
  Courier
VIA ZOOM:

  Senior Management Analyst Public Works Tania Schwartz; Barbara Lazaroff of
  Spago Restaurant; Steve Scott Springer of Spago Restaurant; Ian Dickensen of
  O’Herlihy Architects; Murray Fischer of Beverly Hills Chamber of Commerce; Marc
  Esposito of Signature Party Rentals; Ramsay Edwards-McNear; An unidentified
  person from Caffe Roma; Vicky Mense of Xian; Steve Mayer; Robbie Anderson –
  Resident; Debbie Supnik; Ron Shalowitz; Preston Park; Victor Carina

  1) Public Comment
  a. Members of the public were given the opportunity to directly address the
  Committee on any item listed on the agenda.

    Steve Mayer submitted public comment in advance which was read by
  Magdalena Davis.
    Mark Elliot provided public comment.
 Open BH Design/ Operating Standards Ad Hoc Subcommittee
June 13, 2022
Meeting Highlights

    Robbie Anderson provided public comment.
    Ramsay Edwards-McNear provided public comment.
    Barbara Lazaroff of Spago Restaurant provided public comment.
    Ian Dickenson of O’Herlihy Architects provided public comment.

  2) Resolution of the Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / OpenBH Design and Operating
  Standards Ad Hoc Subcommittee authorizing public meetings to be held via
  teleconferencing pursuant to Government Code Section 54953(e) and making findings
  and determination regarding the same.

  a. New legislation (AB 361) was recently adopted allowing the OpenBH Design and
  Operating Standards Ad Hoc Subcommittee to continue virtual meetings during
  the COVID-19 declared emergency subject to certain conditions and the
  proposed resolution implements the necessary requirements.

    The resolution was read into the record and the Liaisons unanimously
  approved the resolution.

  3) Open BH Design & Operating Standards Subcommitee Stakeholder Outreach Meeting #3

  a. Project History – Mandana Motahari gave a breakdown on the history of the
  Open BH program starting with the temporary necessity caused by the COVID-
  19 pandemic to give restaurants the opportunity to stay operational and to give
  restaurant patrons the opportunity to come out and enjoy outdoor dining within
  the Health Department COVID-19 guidelines. Due to the success of the Open
  BH program and created opportunities for expanded outdoor dining there is a
  strong support to make temporary parklets permanet. The two subcommittees,
  Open BH Design & Operating Standards Ad Hoc Subcommittee and Open BH
  Code Changes and Fees Ad Hoc Subcommittee, along with the critical input from
  the stakeholders, have been created to provide standards and regulations for the
  permanent Open BH program.

  b. Existing Conditions of Parklets – Architect, Lorcan O’Herlihy, spoke about the
  currently existing parklets and how their set up was intended to be temporary and
  does not support long-term use and/or public safety, as well as the elevated
  aesthetics worthy of Beverly Hills. Lorcan discussed the need for compiling the
  framework and standards of the design elements of the parklets along with
  essential stakeholder input and feedback.

  c. Project Goals – Architect/Project Manager, Kevin Murray discussed the research,
  design development, documentation and communication distribution of the work
  plan for development of design guidelines for the new parklets. The presentation
  of a prototype using a kit of parts will be introduced at a future on-site meeting for
  stakeholder assessment and ultimate adoption by the City.

  d. Project Timeline – To take place over the next six months; a four phase plan to
  be delivered to the City in November 2022.
 Open BH Design/ Operating Standards Ad Hoc Subcommittee
June 13, 2022
Meeting Highlights

  e. Small Group Workshop Breakout Sessions

    The group leaders were asked to give the main point(s) of the breakout
  group sessions and came back with the following:

  1. Mondana Motahari – The importance of maintenance of the
  parklets and the utilization of concealed safety elements in the
  design.

  2. Lorcan O’Herlihy – The focus and integration on safety of cars
  and pedestrians in and around the parklets. The desire to keep
  the design as aesthetically welcoming as the rest of Beverly Hills.

  3. Magdalena Davis – The potential possibility to swap the dining
  area with the parklet area, i.e., moving the pedestrian traffic to the
  location that is currently the parklets and aligning the outdoor
  dining tables with the restaurant, creating a “boardwalk style” look.
  The space, style and weather protection features should be
  reflective of the “high end” upscale look of Beverly Hills. Also a
  focus on the manner of concealment of the barriers to provide
  additional safety.

  4. Ian Dickenson – Identifying and applying resiliency to the material,
  to the operation and having each parklet specific design to be
  related to their context.

  f.  Next Steps
    Obtaining feedback and input from stakeholders is very important to the
  success of this program. A web based portal will be provided for
  stakeholders and members of the community to contribute their
  commentary.
    The Open BH comment box will be located at:
  www.beverlyhills.org\openbh.

  4) Future Agenda Items

    The Liaisons will reconvene in approximately one month’s time to
  determine further details.

ADJOURNMENT

  Date / Time: June 13, 2022 / 11:56 AM
